To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CipA enhances the activities of cellulosomal enzymes against crystalline forms of cellulosic substrates by a synergistic mechanism that is not mediated solely by the CipA binding domain.

the Cip A cellulose binding domain (CBD) enhances endoglucanases EGE and E5 activity against crystalline forms of cellulosic substrates by a mechanism that is distinct from its ability to bind to cellulose and that this enhancement is due to the presence of the CBD and not to the ability of EGE or E5 to combine with CipA.

the Cip A cellulose binding domain (CBD) does not mediate the increase in activity solely via bringing the catalytic domains of cellulosomal enzymes into intimate contact with crystalline cellulose, but rather by a mechanism that involves the synergistic interaction between the CBDs of EGE and CipA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of cellulose hydrolysis by the cellulosome of C. thermocellum, a gram-positive bacterium that grows anaerobically on cellulose as the sole carbon and energy source.
the interaction of the CipA protein from Clostridial species with cellulose.
the development of a cellulosome-based biocatalyst to degrade crystalline cellulose to glucose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cellulosome, as a whole, is an extremely efficient system for the hydrolysis of crystalline cellulose, and that the CipC and CipA subcomplexes, which are the major constituents of the cellulosomes, are responsible for the majority of this activity.
CipA enhances the activity of EGE by a mechanism that involves a direct synergistic interaction between EGE and CipA, which is not mediated by CipA binding to cellulose.
CipA acts as a scaffold protein that brings the catalytic domains of the cellulosomal enzymes together in close contact with the crystalline cellulose substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CipA enhances EGE activity on crystalline cellulose by binding to it and by increasing the number of EGE molecules that are in contact with the substrate, but that the CipB binding module of EGE is also important for this activity, and that CipA may enhance EGE activity in part by increasing the number and activity of the CipB modules that are in contact the substrate.
CipA, a protein that is essential for the assembly of cellulosomes, also plays a role in the activity of the cellulosomal enzymes.
CipA is a scaffold protein that organizes the cellulosome and that it is also a synergism factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CipA enhances EGE activity against the crystalline cellulose substrates, Avicel and filter paper, by increasing the rate of cellulose hydrolysis, and not by increasing the rate at which cellulose is degraded to soluble sugars.
a cellulosome subunit can interact synergistically with another cellulosome sub-unit, even if the two are not physically linked.

the CipAs of C. thermocellum and Ruminococcus flavefaciens, and probably other cellulosomal organisms as well, are multifunctional proteins that can bind to cellulose, enhance the catalytic activities of the cellulosomal enzymes that are associated with them, and mediate the assembly of the cellulosomes into a functional complex.
